name: basis Frankfurt
funding: City of Frankfurt Cultural Office (Kulturamt Frankfurt), Hessian Ministry for Science and the Arts; non-profit association.
watch: Non-profit production and exhibition platform in Gutleutviertel; houses over 130 artist studios and international residency exchanges.

name: Beirut Art Center (BAC)
funding: Independent non-profit foundation, cultural grants, community patrons; zero commercial gallery sales.
watch: Sharjah Art Foundation and Qatar Foundation on its patron roll.
why_flagged: Sharjah Art Foundation and Qatar Foundation on its patron roll.
records_note: Annual reports 2009 to 2025 with financial statements are on its site, donors are named by year to 2025, and the board is listed.

name: Belarus Free Theatre
watch: Registered in England 22 May 2012 with its office at the Young Vic, London, and operations in Poland. Trustees per Companies House: Michael Attenborough, Mark Ball, Baroness Helena Kennedy, David Lan, Jude Law, Dame Maria Miller, Alison Stanley, Laura Wade, Samuel West. Producer of 'Official. Unofficial. Belarus' in Venice 2026.
records_note: Companies House holds its full accounts for years to January 2020 to 2025 and its site names eleven trustees; no annual report or funder list.

name: Belarusian Council for Culture (Rada Kultury)
funding: European Union (ArtPower Belarus, €2M over 28 months, delivered with the Danish Cultural Institute); Danish Cultural Institute; listed partners ABBA, RESET!, Forum of National Platforms, NDF
watch: Founded 1 Oct 2020 as the Belarusian Culture Solidarity Fund, renamed Feb 2021; registered in Tallinn as MTÜ Valgevene Kultuuri Assotsiatsioon and represented in Warsaw and Vilnius; CEO Siarhiej Budkin. Reports 1,600+ cultural workers supported and 230+ projects by Oct 2025. Belarus's interior ministry designated it 'extremist' on 7 Jun 2022 and again on 24 Apr 2026.
records_note: It posts activity reports 2021 to 2025 and files accounts in Estonia; partners appear as undated logos, and the site names staff but no board.

name: Belarusian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War
watch: Belarus's most-visited museum, in the 2014 'Victory' building at Praspiekt Pieramožcaŭ 8 (4,200 m2, 10 halls, 8,000+ exhibits shown). Belstat counted 196,700 visitors in 2020, a Covid year; an unsourced figure says about 570,000 a year.
records_note: A state museum under the Ministry of Culture; its site posts no annual reports, accounts or sponsors, and lists only administrators, not a board.

name: Belfast Exposed
funding: Arts Council of Northern Ireland and Belfast City Council, per its support page. A 2024 interview adds trusts and foundations, unnamed.
watch: Both bodies are on the Arts Council NI 2025/26 funding lists. No controversy, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The NI charity register holds its annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; funders show as logos and no board is listed.

name: Bendigo Art Gallery
funding: $45M redevelopment (2025): $21M Victoria, $9M City of Greater Bendigo, Sidney Myer Fund $4M, Ian Potter $3M; partners La Trobe University, Innes, Balgownie, Mercure.
watch: Closed Dec 2025 to early 2028 for redevelopment. A $15M federal Growing Regions bid was rejected Jan 2025 on an administrative issue, not programming.
records_note: bendigoregion.com.au returned HTTP 403; search lists gallery annual reports for 2020 to 2025 and a Gallery Board page, none opened.

name: Berlinische Galerie
funding: Senatsverwaltung für Kultur und Gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt Berlin.
watch: State museum for modern art, photography, and architecture; freelance contractor representation reports.

name: Beta-Local
funding: Mellon Foundation, Andy Warhol Foundation, Arts Collaboratory, independent donations; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Non-profit artist-run organization, La Práctica study program, and El Ivan Illich community school in Old San Juan.
records_note: Names current and past funders on its about page, undated; Form 990s for 2014 to 2023 sit on ProPublica; no annual report or board list.

name: Bétonsalon – Centre d'art et de recherche
funding: City of Paris, DRAC Île-de-France (French Ministry of Culture), Université Paris Cité; certified clean public trust.

name: Beursschouwburg
funding: Flemish Community, Flemish Community Commission (VGC); non-profit multidisciplinary cultural house.

name: Bienal de Arte Paiz
funding: 24th edition (2025-26) run by Fundación Paiz; founder money from the Paiz retail family.
records_note: Neither the Bienal nor Fundación Paiz posts a report, accounts or donor list; the foundation page names only its board president, María Regina Paiz.
